## Identification of Data Sources

<!-- Describe what data is available and where it comes from. -->
The table below summarizes the data sources used in this project, 
detailing their type, time span, granularity, system of record (SoR), and content. 
All data is sourced from SAP BI, which extracts it from the underlying 
systems of record. 
The table also lists the specific SAP tables used for each data source.

```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-sources
#| tbl-cap: "Overview of data sources used in the project"
#| results: 'asis'

# Read the data into a data.table 
dtDS <-  fread(text = "
  Data Source, Type, Time-Span, Granularity, SoR   , Table, Content
  article    , MD  ,          ,            , SAP S4, MARC , article attr.  & hierachy
  customer   , MD  ,          ,            , SAP S4, KNVV , customer attr. hierachy
  sales      , TD  , > 2020   , daily      , SAP S4, LIPS , customer orders + free-of-charge 
  forecasts  , TD  , > 2023   , monhtly    , QAD   ,      , monthly pre- & post Demand review forecasts
")

# Create a styled kableExtra table
dtDS %>% 
  kbl(
    # caption             = "Overview of data sources used in the project",
    col.names           = names(.),
    align               = "l",
    booktabs            = TRUE
  ) %>% 
  kable_styling(
    full_width          = FALSE,
    position            = "left",
    bootstrap_options   = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")
  )  %>%
  add_footnote(
    label    = "MD = Master Data, TD = Transaction Data",
    notation = "none"
  )
```

### Articles

The Article Master Data is extracted from `MARC` which contains Plant specific 
data, this is enhanced with sales organization specific data from `MVKE` and 
global article data from `MARA`.  
The following filters are applied:

```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-sources-article-filters
#| echo: false
#| caption: "Article Master Data Filters"

dtAF <-  fread(text = "
  FIELD      , Filter                        , Reason
  MARA-MTART , HAWA; FERT; VOLL              , only finished goods
  MARA-STRGRP, Z1                            , only Make-to-Stock   
  MVKE-PRAT7 , not 'X'                       , exclude Promotions (fixed planned)
  MARC-DISMM , ZC; ZD; ZG; ZH; ZI; ZJ; ZN; ZP, only MRP relevant
  MARC-PERKZ , W                             , only Ambient
  ")

# Create a styled kableExtra table
dtAF %>% 
  kbl(
    caption             = "Article Master Data Filters",
    col.names           = names(.),
    align               = "l",
    booktabs            = TRUE
  ) %>% 
  kable_styling(
    full_width          = FALSE,
    position            = "left",
    bootstrap_options   = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    latex_options       = c("striped", "hold_position")    
  )
```

see @sec-01-bu-scope for reasons for article-filters.


### Customers

Customer Master Data is sourced from `KNVV`, which contains sales-organization-specific information, and is enriched with global attributes from `KNA1`. This includes customer classification fields such as type (e.g., internal, external, one-time customer, or employee). Customers flagged as employees are excluded from the analysis.

### Sales
<!-- Data filters applied (Doctype's, Item category, ...) -->
<!-- exclude Promotion articles --> PRAT7

Sales data is extracted from `LIPS`, which contains delivery records. Only completed deliveries related to standard sales orders and free-of-charge transactions are included in the analysis.
The following filters are applied:

```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-sources-sales-filters
#| echo: false
#| caption: "Sales Data Filters"

dtSF <-  fread(text = "
  FIELD      , Filter                        , Reason

  ")

# Create a styled kableExtra table
dtSF %>% 
  kbl(
    caption             = "Sales Data Filters",
    col.names           = names(.),
    align               = "l",
    booktabs            = TRUE
  ) %>% 
  kable_styling(
    full_width          = FALSE,
    position            = "left",
    bootstrap_options   = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
    latex_options       = c("striped", "hold_position")    
  )
```

### Forecasts

Forecasts are generated monthly for each article–plant–customer combination, with a planning horizon of up to three years. For this research, the focus is on the year 2024, using a forecast horizon of up to 12 months. Consequently, only forecasts generated from 2023 onward are considered.

Since forecasts are created both before and after the Demand Review, the dataset is split into two versions: *pre-Demand Review* and *post-Demand Review*. The pre-Demand Review forecasts are used for the initial analysis, while the post-Demand Review forecasts serve as the basis for final validation.

## Data Collection Report
<!-- Summarize how data was obtained and any issues during acquisition: -->

All data is Sourced from *BioBalance* SAP-BI system using the SAP Open Hub Technology.

![Data Collection pipelines](../images/dp01.png){#dp01 fig-align="center"}

###Data Flow

1. The data is extracted from the Production SAP system, using the Open-Hub
   technology and stored on One-drive in the Bronze layer of the stageing area, 
   following the medallion structure.
2. One-Drive synchronizes the data to get it available for the 
   System-of-Innovation: Pythia's Advice.    
3. An in-process duckDB session is used to read the csv-files and convert these to parquet while
   applying the necessary light transformations. This data is stored in the 
   Silver layer of the staging area.

```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-collection

# Read the data into a data.table 
dtDC <-  fread(text = "
  Data Source         , Type, Extract Date, Records, GB  , Key
  article master data , MD  ,             ,        ,     , Article     
  customer master data, MD  ,             ,        ,     , Customer
  historical sales    , TD  ,             ,        ,     , Date; Article; Plant; Customer
  historical forecasts, TD  ,             ,        ,     , Date; Article; Plant; CustHier3
")

# Create a styled kableExtra table
dtDC %>% 
  kbl(
    caption             = "Data Collection ",
    col.names           = names(.),
    align               = "l",
    booktabs            = TRUE
  ) %>% 
  kable_styling(
    full_width          = FALSE,
    position            = "left",
    bootstrap_options   = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")
  )
```

## Transformations

Light transformations are applied to the exported CSV files. These include renaming fields, converting data types, formatting date fields, and adding leading zeros where required. Additionally, a new variable is calculated to capture the number of months between the forecast creation date and the forecasted period.

<!-- DuckDB tranformations -->
```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-db-transformations
dtTF <- pa_transformations_get() %>%
  .[, POSIT:= NULL]
```

```{r}
#| label: tab-02-data-description-hierarchy

OD <- "C:\\Users\\flori\\OneDrive\\ET\\pythia\\data"

# Read the data into a data.table
dtMAT <- wb_read(
  file      = file.path(OD, "ET2BB.xlsx"),
  sheet     = "MASP",
  start_row = 19,
  start_col = 6,
  skip_empty_cols = TRUE,
  skip_empty_rows = TRUE
) %T>%
  setDT() %T>%
  setnames(
    c(4, 6, 8, 9), 
    c("ProdCat", "SubCat", "Family", "Article")
  ) %>%
  .[, .(ProdCat, SubCat, Family, Article)] %>%
  unique()

dtCUST <- wb_read(
  file      = file.path(OD, "ET2BB.xlsx"),
  sheet     = "CUST",
  start_row = 19,
  start_col = 9,
  skip_empty_cols = TRUE,
  skip_empty_rows = TRUE
) %T>%
  setDT() %T>%
  setnames(c(1), c("KEY")  ) 

dtCUST_H1 <- wb_read(
  file      = file.path(OD, "ET2BB.xlsx"),
  sheet     = "CUST_H1",
  start_row = 1,
  start_col = 1,
  skip_empty_cols = TRUE,
  skip_empty_rows = TRUE
) %T>%
  setDT() %T>%
  setnames(c(1), c("KEY")  )

dtCST <- 
  dtCUST_H1[dtCUST, on = .(KEY), nomatch = 0] %T>%
  setnames(
    c(4, 7, 9, 11),
    c("Channel", "Key_Account", "Account", "SoldTo")
  ) %>%
  .[, .(Channel, Key_Account, Account, SoldTo, Customer)] %>%
  unique()
```
